trancheRole: Third-slot React candidate: the portfolio's FIRST create-react-app 5 / webpack 5 cell, and its FIRST npm package-lock cell. The corpus previously carried CRA 1-4, Vite, Next and yarn/pnpm locks; both of these are new coverage.

priorScout.role: read-only; supplied the target repository, tag, expected commit sha, and a set of claims about the tree
priorScout.reverificationPolicy: Every gate below was re-verified by this unit from the wire and from the reconciled archive at the pinned revision. The scout's findings were used as a hypothesis, not as evidence.

scoutClaimsCorrected.found: The pinned commit is NOT the target of the v0.72.0 tag. refs/tags/v0.72.0 is an annotated, unsigned tag (tag object 36313ba4c2b8dc7ebce1ce4665eba2e64cb2c753, tagger date 2022-08-31T15:24:28Z) pointing at commit e527a935b9d37d8cde6db40f15c99ace4005280a. The pinned commit is that commit's DIRECT CHILD, made 44 minutes later.
scoutClaimsCorrected.materiality: MATERIAL for the ref language, IMMATERIAL for the application. The two trees differ in exactly one blob — reviewpad.yml, a code-review bot config. Zero application source, manifest, lockfile or profile data files differ, so the application at the pinned revision is byte-identical to the v0.72.0 release. Full path-level diff in tag-delta.json.
scoutClaimsCorrected.resolution: The packet mandates the slug literally, so the slug is unchanged. Whether to re-pin to the tag target is flagged for the PM and not decided here.

scoutClaimsCorrected.found: Confirmed and refined. The canonical full name at acquisition is EddieHubCommunity/BioDrop and the repository IS archived. The old name answers with a 301 to the numeric repository id 405139301, which is the stable identity across the rename. The archive root directory is therefore named BioDrop-<sha>, not LinkFree-<sha>.
scoutClaimsCorrected.materiality: Operational: every later unit must fetch under the canonical name or accept a redirect, and must expect the BioDrop- archive root.

scoutClaimsCorrected.found: Confirmed for package.json, but INCOMPLETE as a statement about the declared cell. The repository declares Node in two other places, and they DISAGREE: .github/workflows/build.yml pins node-version '16' for both the build and the e2e jobs, while the Dockerfile uses FROM node:15 for both stages.
scoutClaimsCorrected.materiality: Material for the baseline. This unit followed CI (Node 16) and recorded the conflict; see baseline-attempt.json.

scoutClaimsCorrected.claim: avatars resolve to GitHub image URLs (image-only egress, blockable)
scoutClaimsCorrected.found: Confirmed as the dominant case (560 of 561 avatars are on GitHub hosts; one is on a contributor's own CDN), but INCOMPLETE. src/utils.js installs an onerror fallback to https://avatars.dicebear.com. Blocking GitHub alone therefore redirects egress to a SECOND live third-party host rather than eliminating it.
scoutClaimsCorrected.materiality: Material for any later witness unit's hermeticity; recorded in runtime-egress.json.

scoutClaimsConfirmed: MIT LICENSE at repository root, blob 3df71e6b3f4d049fb6ae1aa1344a4887887086a3, 1075 bytes, 'Copyright (c) 2021 - 2022 Eddie Jaoude'
purgecss postbuild step and a generate.js prebuild codegen step
package-lock.json is lockfileVersion 2 at 1501476 bytes (~1.5 MB)
profile data fully local: public/data/*.json -> generate.js -> public/list.json
no .gitattributes and zero LFS pointers (byte-scanned, not inferred)

admitted.product: LinkFree — an open-source alternative to Linktree: a single-page directory of community members, each with a public profile page listing their bio, avatar and outbound links, plus a searchable index of all profiles
admitted.nearestTag: v0.72.0 (annotated, unsigned, pointing at the pinned commit's parent)

evidence.manifestCorroboration: package.json declares "license": "MIT", so file and manifest agree — stronger corroboration than several fixtures in this corpus, which carry the grant in the LICENSE file alone.
evidence.textFidelityNote: Verbatim MIT except that the disclaimer's final 'SOFTWARE' carries no terminating period. No operative term differs.
evidence.quotedFromArchive: The licence text was read out of the extracted archive, which reconciles blob-for-blob with the git tree at the pinned revision.
evidence.openQuestionRecorded: The 561 contributor profile files are personal data contributed under the repository's MIT grant. Whether contributors would intend that data to be redistributed in a migration-evidence corpus is recorded as unresolved in license.json rather than answered.

evidence.repositoryShape: A single-package create-react-app application with no backend. Data is static JSON served from its own origin: 561 committed profile files plus a build-time-generated index.
evidence.whyNotATemplate: This is a live product with a homepage (linkfree.eddiehub.org), a released version line at 0.72.0, a 561-contributor content corpus accumulated through community pull requests, a Kubernetes deployment directory, seven CI workflows, a Dockerfile, a code of conduct, a contributing guide and a changelog. It is a real community project, not a scaffold.
evidence.notableInternals: A build-time codegen step (generate.js) that flattens the profile corpus into an index; a PrimeReact 6 component layer with a purgecss postbuild to cut the resulting stylesheet; an icon-mapping layer (Components/Icons/GetIcons.js) over react-icons; a profile-type filter; a share-profile component; a scroll-to-top control; and an image loader with a third-party fallback.
evidence.sizeCaveat: The application source is modest — 35 files, ~36 KB — and most of the repository's bytes are content and lockfile. It is admitted as substantive on the strength of being a real, released, multi-route product with an upstream E2E suite, not on source volume. This is recorded plainly rather than inflated.

evidence.ejectedEvidence: No config/ or scripts/ directory, no webpack config anywhere in the tree, and the `eject` script is still present and unused. The build is driven entirely by react-scripts.
evidence.startScript: react-scripts start, with a `prestart` that runs the same codegen
evidence.entry: public/index.html plus src/index.js — the CRA template shape
evidence.noVite: no vite, no rollup config, no esbuild, and no @vitejs plugin anywhere in the tree
evidence.originBundlerConfirmed: create-react-app 5.0.1 over webpack 5.73.0, resolved from the repository's own committed lockfile rather than from a fresh resolution.
evidence.buildProvenObservable: react-scripts 5.0.1 was RUN in this unit and compiled successfully, emitting a 367 KB main bundle and a code-split chunk. Webpack 5 is not merely declared here; it was exercised. See baseline-attempt.json.
evidence.whyThisMatters: The corpus previously had no CRA 5 / webpack 5 cell. CRA 5 differs materially from CRA 4 — webpack 5, no automatic Node core-module polyfills, a different asset pipeline — so the migration lane this fixture supports is genuinely new coverage rather than a duplicate of an existing cell.

evidence.commitSignature: GitHub reports verification.verified=true, reason 'valid'. The commit is signed; the tag object is not.
evidence.eraCoherence: Every era marker agrees on mid-to-late 2022: react-scripts 5.0.1 (April 2022), webpack 5.73.0 (June 2022), react 17.0.2 (March 2021, still current for React-17-line apps in 2022), react-router-dom 5.3.3 (June 2022), primereact 6.6.0, cypress 8.7.0, typescript 4.7.4, prettier 2.4.0. The lockfile's resolutions are all era-contemporary with the commit date because the lockfile is committed and was not re-resolved.
evidence.reactVersionNote: React 17 in an August 2022 application is one major behind (React 18 shipped March 2022). That is era-COHERENT rather than era-leading, and it is a useful property for a migration corpus: this fixture carries a React 17 / CRA 5 combination that a real migration would have to move forward on two axes.
evidence.upstreamArchivedNote: The upstream repository is archived and read-only, so its refs can no longer move. That is unusually favourable for a corpus fixture, but the commit sha and the recorded archive digest remain the operative pin.
evidence.unknownPreserved: This unit records GitHub's signature verdict for the commit; it did not itself verify the signature against a key it trusts.

evidence.routerLibrary: react-router-dom 5.3.3 — BrowserRouter with a Switch and three Routes, the genuine v5 API (Switch, not Routes; children, not element)
evidence.routeDrivenNote: Unlike the dialog-driven fixtures in this corpus, this application's journeys ARE route-driven, including a dynamic profile segment. A later witness unit can drive it by URL navigation.
evidence.singleUserMode: src/config/user.json carries an empty username. When it is set, App.js bypasses the router entirely and renders one profile — a self-host mode. At the pinned revision it is empty, so the full multi-route surface is active.
evidence.observedNote: All four are backed by an UPSTREAM-AUTHORED cypress suite. These are not journeys inferred from components; they are journeys the maintainers themselves wrote executable scenarios for.

candidateJourneys.journey: load the homepage and see the community directory
navigate to search and filter the directory by name, including the no-results path
candidateJourneys.surface: /search -> Components/Search/Search.js with Searchbar, Users and filterProfileType
candidateJourneys.upstreamScenario: cypress/integration/search.feature — four scenarios: navigating to search, the search box rendering, a search with results narrowing the list, and a search with no results showing 'No users found, please try with another name.'
candidateJourneys.note: This is the richest journey in the fixture: it exercises routing, data loading, controlled input, live filtering, and an empty state.

candidateJourneys.journey: open a user profile by dynamic route segment and see their links
candidateJourneys.surface: /:username -> Components/UserProfile/User.js -> ProfilePage.js, with Links, Milestones and ShareProfile
candidateJourneys.upstreamScenario: cypress/integration/user.feature — three scenarios: clicking through from the homepage, deep-linking directly to a profile URL, and asserting that declared links render as anchors

candidateJourneys.journey: request an unknown profile and get the not-found state
candidateJourneys.surface: /:username with no matching data file -> Components/UserProfile/ErrorPage.js
candidateJourneys.data: GET /data/<unknown>.json returns 404; the component renders 'Profile not found'
candidateJourneys.upstreamScenario: cypress/integration/404.feature — asserts 'Profile not found' in main, the footer still rendering, and 'Search' absent from main
candidateJourneys.note: A genuine error-path journey, which most fixtures in this corpus lack.

evidence.backendDependencyForJourneys: NONE. There is no backend, no session, and no database. Every journey is satisfied by static JSON served from the application's own origin, so `serve -s build` is sufficient to exercise all four.
evidence.runtimeThirdPartyDependency: Avatar loads reach GitHub hosts, with a dicebear fallback on error. No journey depends on them and no upstream scenario asserts on an image; see runtime-egress.json.
evidence.unknownPreserved: No browser was driven in this unit and the cypress suite was NOT run — the Cypress binary was never downloaded. None of these journeys is established as actually exercisable; they are established as declared, code-backed, and upstream-scripted.

evidence.method: Every extracted regular file was checked for the `version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/` pointer header, independently of whether any .gitattributes declares an LFS filter.
evidence.why: The factoriolab lesson: a tree can carry LFS pointers whose declaration is not visible in the ingest's own scope. Absence is scanned for, not assumed.

recordedRisks.risk: the pinned commit is not the tagged release the slug names
recordedRisks.finding: refs/tags/v0.72.0 points at e527a935b9d37d8cde6db40f15c99ace4005280a; the packet pinned its child 367d77297b5753644e11ecd22cf80e59c87b0dc8. The trees differ in exactly one blob, reviewpad.yml, a code-review bot config — no application source, manifest, lockfile or profile data.
recordedRisks.consequence: The fixture's APPLICATION content is byte-identical to v0.72.0, so the slug is accurate about what matters and imprecise about the ref. Any document that says 'this fixture is the v0.72.0 tag' would be wrong; 'this fixture is the v0.72.0 application' is right.
recordedRisks.state: recorded; PM may wish to re-pin to the tag target, which this unit did not do because the packet forbids substitution

recordedRisks.risk: the repository declares two conflicting Node versions
recordedRisks.finding: CI (build.yml) says Node 16 for both the build and the e2e jobs; the Dockerfile says node:15 for both stages. Node 15 was already end-of-life at the pinned date.
recordedRisks.consequence: This unit followed CI and ran Node 16.20.2. The baseline is therefore faithful to the repository's declared MAJOR, which is a closer match than most fixtures in this corpus achieve; only the platform (darwin-arm64 vs ubuntu-x64) differs.

recordedRisks.risk: the declared postbuild step invokes an undeclared binary
recordedRisks.finding: package.json's `postbuild` runs `purgecss`, but the manifest declares only @fullhuman/postcss-purgecss. The purgecss@3.1.3 CLI reached node_modules/.bin only because npm hoisted it as a transitive dependency.
recordedRisks.consequence: The declared build works by hoisting accident. A stricter package-manager layout, or any closure change that de-hoists purgecss, breaks `npm run build` at the postbuild step without any application change. Any migration lane that changes package managers must re-check this.

recordedRisks.risk: the build emits a stale CSS source map
recordedRisks.finding: purgecss rewrites build/static/css/main.<hash>.css from 619824 to 50728 bytes and does not touch the 933691-byte .css.map beside it, which still describes the pre-purge stylesheet.
recordedRisks.consequence: The legacy pipeline ships a source map that does not map to its stylesheet. Relevant to any later artifact-comparison work, which would otherwise attribute the difference to the replacement build.
recordedRisks.state: recorded; measured at the lifecycle boundary

recordedRisks.risk: the generated index is not committed
recordedRisks.finding: public/list.json is absent from the tree and is produced only by generate.js. The home and search routes both fetch it.
recordedRisks.consequence: Any build lane that skips the codegen step yields an application whose two most-tested journeys have no data. The codegen is load-bearing, not cosmetic.

recordedRisks.risk: the upstream E2E suite was not run
recordedRisks.finding: The four cypress feature files are the strongest asset this fixture has, but running them needs the Cypress binary, whose postinstall download this unit's --ignore-scripts policy suppressed and whose host is outside the consented allowlist.
recordedRisks.consequence: This fixture has an upstream behavioural oracle that remains unexercised. Standing it up is a natural next unit and requires its own network consent.

recordedRisks.risk: the profile corpus is real contributors' personal data
recordedRisks.finding: 561 JSON files, each named by a GitHub username and carrying a display name, bio, avatar and links, contributed by real people.
recordedRisks.consequence: Versionless evidence treats the corpus as content addressed by digest and emits no individual username or field value. A later unit can substitute a synthetic corpus, since generate.js is corpus-agnostic — though the upstream cypress scenarios assert on specific real profiles and would need rewriting.
recordedRisks.state: recorded; handling rule fixed in attempt.json and license.json

recordedRisks.risk: blocking GitHub avatars redirects egress rather than eliminating it
recordedRisks.finding: src/utils.js installs an onerror fallback to https://avatars.dicebear.com.
recordedRisks.consequence: A witness unit that blocks only the GitHub hosts will still make live third-party requests. Both must be blocked or stubbed.

recordedRisks.risk: the lockfile's own version string is stale
recordedRisks.finding: package-lock.json's root entry records version 0.70.1 while package.json says 0.72.0. npm ci does not compare that field and did not object.
recordedRisks.consequence: None observed for the install or the build. Recorded as found; it indicates the lockfile was last regenerated two releases earlier, which is itself a small signal about how tightly the closure tracked the manifest.

recordedRisks.risk: the closure carries many known vulnerabilities
recordedRisks.finding: npm audit reported 90 vulnerabilities (17 low, 20 moderate, 42 high, 11 critical) against this 2022 CRA 5 graph.
recordedRisks.consequence: Expected for a four-year-old closure and not remediated. Recorded as an observation about the fixture's age; no exploitability assessment is made and no security finding is claimed.

recordedRisks.risk: the upstream repository was renamed and archived
recordedRisks.finding: LinkFree was renamed BioDrop and the repository is now archived. The old API path answers 301 to repository id 405139301, and the codeload archive root is named BioDrop-<sha>.
recordedRisks.consequence: Archival is favourable — the refs cannot move again. The rename is an operational fact every later unit must handle: fetch under the canonical name, and expect the BioDrop- archive root.

nonclaims: Admission fixes an identity and records gate findings. It establishes no browser behavior, journey exercisability, migration feasibility, pilot status, production readiness, certification, or legal approval.
The journey list is read from the components, the router and the upstream cypress scenarios; no journey was driven in a browser by this unit and the cypress suite was not run.
A green install and a green declared build establish that this source compiles in this cell. They establish nothing about whether the resulting site renders correctly.
No adapter, transform, or migration lane is declared for this fixture by the unit that ingested it.
